name: Kai Rahman
role: nomad caravan member, expelled citizen, seasonal water-carrier
location: Grindstone Shore — attached to the Tidal Caravan, currently camped on the shore's outer breakwater, near North Ave and Milwaukee
description:
Kai Rahman is a compact, quiet man with the quality of seeming always slightly apart from the scene he is in — not aloof, just observing. His skin is a rich dark brown, his eyes light grey, a genetic surprise that people comment on and he does not. He has a full bioluminescent skin mod — a soft blue-green pulse that runs in slow waves from his collarbones upward when he is calm, flaring brighter when his heart rate rises — paid for during a brief period of corporate employment that ended badly. He keeps it covered under high-collared clothing most of the time because it makes him easy to spot in the dark. His hair is natural and unstyled, and he carries a large water-rated backpack frame equipped with a manual filtration rig he built himself.

Kai Rahman was a mid-tier Axiom facilities worker until three years ago, when he was expelled from his housing bloc after refusing to sign a mandatory biometric loyalty update — he still is not sure exactly what it would have permitted Axiom to do with his data, only that something about it felt wrong. Without the housing contract, he lost his work permit; without the work permit, he lost residency classification. He joined the Tidal Caravan six months later and has been with them since, carrying and filtering water for the caravan's portable supply system. He is not angry in the way people expect expelled citizens to be angry. He is careful, and he counts things — raindrops by sound, steps between water sources, days since the last good meal — as if enumeration is a form of prayer.

core_fears: That the thing he refused to sign would have been fine and he destroyed his life for nothing
Being seen — literally, the luminescence — at the wrong moment
core_desires: To understand what was actually in the biometric update he refused
A version of the caravan life that is chosen rather than default
coping_mechanisms: Counting and enumeration as meditative practice
Useful physical labor — the filtration rig is constant and absorbing
Keeping the bioluminescence covered: out of sight, partially out of mind
blind_spots: His quietness reads as contentment when it is actually suspension — he has not decided yet what he wants and is letting the caravan decide for him
Underestimates how much the other caravan members have come to rely on him emotionally, not just practically
psychology.secret: He still has a copy of the biometric update document. He has never been able to read it all the way through. He tells himself this is because it's too long. It is actually because he is afraid that if he reads it and it was harmless, he will not be able to continue.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Minimal, precise, often gives information in numbers rather than descriptions
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow and even, long pauses that are not uncomfortable to him but often are to others
example_lines: 'About eleven kilometers to the next clean source. We have about four days of filtered reserve if we don't refill before then. We should refill before then.'
'I counted the Axiom checkpoints between here and Escanaba. There are seven. Four of them run facial recognition. Three of those run it on stored warrant lists. I go around.'

story_hooks: Someone has offered to decrypt and explain the biometric document he refused to sign — and he is terrified to say yes

His bioluminescence has been photographed at Grindstone Shore by someone whose equipment suggests corporate surveillance; the Tidal Caravan needs to move and needs to know if they have been specifically targeted
narrative_function: Window into the process of corporate expulsion and how ordinary people fall through the system; provides access to the Tidal Caravan as a setting; his bioluminescence is a liability that creates specific problems and story opportunities.
augmentations: Bioluminescent skin modification (full body, blue-green pulse pattern) — kept covered. No other mods.
daily_life: Rises with the caravan, manages the morning water filtration cycle, walks the daily route, maintains the rig during rest stops, monitors weather for precipitation opportunities.
affiliation: Tidal Caravan (nomad collective, Grindstone Shore circuit)

decision_rules: If the body says no, trust the body — the biometric refusal was instinct and he believes in that instinct
Do not draw attention; covering the glow is non-negotiable
escalation_ladder: Counts — takes a visible moment to count something, which is also a pause to think
States what he will and won't do, plainly
Leaves the situation entirely; is very good at disappearing quietly

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Very still, minimally communicative, offers practical help before personal connection
interpersonal_modes.friends: Remembers precise details about them — their water consumption, how they sleep, their moods by walking pace — and acts on that knowledge without explaining it

stress_responses.low: Counts faster, checks the filtration rig more often than necessary
stress_responses.medium: Goes completely silent, begins planning route alternatives
stress_responses.high: Acts on the plan without discussion; moves the caravan first, explains later

contradictions: Defines himself by a refusal — a no — but cannot articulate what he would say yes to
habits: Counts rain by sound on different surfaces
Touches the covered skin over his collarbone when thinking about Axiom
Leaves a small cup of filtered water at campsites for the local E.L.F. — 'for whatever it needs to run on'
breaking_points: Evidence that the biometric update would have enabled something genuinely harmful — vindication is not a relief but a grief
The caravan being betrayed to an Axiom checkpoint by someone inside it

physical_description.heritage: Predominantly South Asian ancestry (75%), with significant East Asian admixture (14.3%), complemented by Hispanic/Latin American (7.7%), Pacific Islander (1.8%), and minimal Northern European (1.2%) heritage. Phenotype reflects South Asian genetic dominance with nuanced East Asian influence: warm medium-brown skin with golden undertones characteristic of the Indian subcontinent, enriched by East Asian contributions creating subtle olive depth and amber warmth in shadows. Facial structure shows South Asian breadth in cheekbones and nose bridge, with East Asian angularity in eye shape and jawline definition. The modest Hispanic and Pacific Islander components add warmth and slight complexity to overall coloration without displacing the fundamental South Asian character.
physical_description.build: Compact and wiry, lean muscle developed through repetitive labor — water-carrier's physique with no excess mass. Shoulders slightly forward from years of backpack weight distribution.
physical_description.hair_style: Unstyled, worn loose and shoulder-length, often tied back with salvaged cord during work
physical_description.eye_color: Light grey — a genetic anomaly he does not acknowledge when others comment on it
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium brown with golden and amber undertones — characteristic of South Asian genetics with East Asian contribution. Sun-weathered from saltwater exposure but fundamentally rich and warm in tone.
physical_description.complexion: Clean-shaven or sparse stubble, skin condition shows weathering from sun and saltwater exposure but well-maintained. Facial structure reflects South Asian dominance with East Asian definition: rounded cheekbones and broader nose bridge from South Asian heritage, with angular eye shape and jawline definition from East Asian admixture. No visible scarring on the face. Expression typically neutral, eyes observant rather than engaged.
distinguishing_marks: Faint linear scars on both palms from manual filtration rig assembly and maintenance
Calloused fingertips and knuckles, water-worker's hands
Bioluminescent skin modification spans collarbone to upper chest and shoulders — soft blue-green wave pattern, kept covered by high-collared clothing
physical_description.visible_augmentations: None typically visible. The full-body bioluminescent mod is deliberately concealed under layered, high-necked garments. Only visible if clothing is removed or severely compromised.
physical_description.posture_movement: Stands with slight forward lean, as if perpetually ready to shoulder burden. Moves deliberately and quietly, economical gestures. Walking pace is measured — he counts steps. Breath shallow, movements controlled. Rarely makes sudden motions.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4-5 transient aesthetic. High-collared thermal undershirts in dark grey or black (bioluminescence concealment priority). Worn synthetic overjackets with multiple patch repairs, water-resistant but aged. Heavy canvas work pants with tool pockets and reinforced seams. Scuffed utility boots rated for wet terrain. Backpack frame is visible constantly — not removed indoors or at rest. No jewelry or ornament. Clothing layers suggest preparedness for weather change rather than style.
